1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_server.c
3:  *
4:  * The socket half of the provisioning entry.  Deliberately POSIX-only so the
5:  * accept loop, the ordering guarantee and one-shot mode can be exercised over
6:  * loopback on the host; the only thing left for the board is whether the
7:  * SoftAP and SD-NAND are actually there.
8:  *
9:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #include <arpa/inet.h>
13: #include <errno.h>
14: #include <netinet/in.h>
15: #include <poll.h>
16: #include <pthread.h>
17: #include <stdbool.h>
18: #include <stdio.h>
19: #include <string.h>
20: #include <sys/socket.h>
21: #include <unistd.h>
22: 
23: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
24: #include "vp_form.h"
25: #include "vp_http.h"
26: #include "vp_store.h"
27: 
28: #define VP_STATE_IDLE     0
29: #define VP_STATE_RUNNING  1
30: #define VP_STATE_FINISHED 2  /* the thread returned, still needs a join */
31: 
32: #define VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS  200
33: #define VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 5000
34: #define VP_STORE_PATH_MAX  192
35: #define VP_THREAD_STACK    8192
36: 
37: struct vp_server_s
38: {
39:   int       listenfd;
40:   pthread_t thread;
41:   int       state;
42:   bool      stopping;
43:   bool      one_shot;
44:   char      store_path[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];
45:   uint32_t  generation;
46:   velasight_prov_saved_cb_t on_saved;
47:   void     *cb_arg;
48: };
49: 
50: static struct vp_server_s g_server =
51: {
52:   .listenfd = -1,
53:   .state    = VP_STATE_IDLE,
54: };
55: 
56: static pthread_mutex_t g_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
57: 
58: /* Request and response buffers are static because only one connection is
59:  * served at a time and 6KB of thread stack on this part is not free.
60:  */
61: 
62: static char g_request[VP_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS + VP_HTTP_MAX_BODY + 1];
63: static char g_response[VP_HTTP_RESPONSE_MAX];
64: 
65: static int vp_write_all(int fd, const char *data, size_t len)
66: {
67:   size_t sent = 0;
68: 
69:   while (sent < len)
70:     {
71:       ssize_t n = write(fd, data + sent, len - sent);
72: 
73:       if (n < 0)
74:         {
75:           if (errno == EINTR)
76:             {
77:               continue;
78:             }
79: 
80:           return -errno;
81:         }
82: 
83:       if (n == 0)
84:         {
85:           return -EPIPE;
86:         }
87: 
88:       sent += (size_t)n;
89:     }
90: 
91:   return 0;
92: }
93: 
94: /****************************************************************************
95:  * Name: vp_read_request
96:  *
97:  * Description:
98:  *   Read until the headers plus the declared body have arrived, the cap is
99:  *   reached or the deadline passes.  Returns the total length, or negative on
100:  *   error.  A client that opens a connection and says nothing costs one
101:  *   timeout, not the service.
102:  *
103:  ****************************************************************************/
104: 
105: static int vp_read_request(int fd, struct vp_http_request_s *req)
106: {
107:   size_t total = 0;
108:   int waited = 0;
109: 
110:   for (; ; )
111:     {
112:       struct pollfd pfd;
113:       ssize_t n;
114:       int ret;
115: 
116:       ret = vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req);
117:       if (ret == 0)
118:         {
119:           if (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
120:               total >= req->header_len + req->content_length)
121:             {
122:               return (int)total;
123:             }
124:         }
125:       else if (ret != -EAGAIN)
126:         {
127:           return ret;
128:         }
129: 
130:       if (total >= sizeof(g_request) - 1)
131:         {
132:           return -E2BIG;
133:         }
134: 
135:       pfd.fd = fd;
136:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
137:       pfd.revents = 0;
138:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
139:       if (ret < 0)
140:         {
141:           if (errno == EINTR)
142:             {
143:               continue;
144:             }
145: 
146:           return -errno;
147:         }
148: 
149:       if (ret == 0)
150:         {
151:           waited += VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS;
152:           if (waited >= VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
153:             {
154:               return -ETIMEDOUT;
155:             }
156: 
157:           continue;
158:         }
159: 
160:       n = read(fd, g_request + total, sizeof(g_request) - 1 - total);
161:       if (n < 0)
162:         {
163:           if (errno == EINTR)
164:             {
165:               continue;
166:             }
167: 
168:           return -errno;
169:         }
170: 
171:       if (n == 0)
172:         {
173:           /* Peer closed.  Whatever arrived is all there will be, so let the
174:            * parser decide between "incomplete" and "answerable".
175:            */
176: 
177:           if (vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req) == 0 &&
178:               (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
179:                total >= req->header_len + req->content_length))
180:             {
181:               return (int)total;
182:             }
183: 
184:           return -ECONNRESET;
185:         }
186: 
187:       total += (size_t)n;
188:     }
189: }
190: 
191: /****************************************************************************
192:  * Name: vp_handle
193:  *
194:  * Description:
195:  *   Serve one connection.  Sets *saved when credentials were persisted and
196:  *   *save_status to 0 or the negative errno of a failed save, so the caller can
197:  *   notify the application only after the socket is gone.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: static void vp_handle(int fd, bool *saved, int *save_status,
202:                       uint32_t *generation)
203: {
204:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
205:   struct vp_http_request_s req;
206:   size_t len = 0;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   *saved = false;
210:   *save_status = 0;
211: 
212:   ret = vp_read_request(fd, &req);
213:   if (ret < 0)
214:     {
215:       if (ret == -E2BIG)
216:         {
217:           len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 431,
218:                                     "请求过大。");
219:         }
220:       else
221:         {
222:           /* Nothing usable arrived; answering a client that already gave up
223:            * is not worth a second syscall.
224:            */
225: 
226:           return;
227:         }
228:     }
229:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_PAGE)
230:     {
231:       len = vp_http_form_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), NULL);
232:     }
233:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_REJECT)
234:     {
235:       len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), req.status,
236:                                req.status == 404 ? "页面不存在。" :
237:                                req.status == 405 ? "不支持该请求方法。" :
238:                                req.status == 413 ? "提交内容过大。" :
239:                                req.status == 415 ? "提交格式不受支持。" :
240:                                req.status == 411 ? "缺少 Content-Length。" :
241:                                                    "请求无法解析。");
242:     }
243:   else
244:     {
245:       memset(&cred, 0, sizeof(cred));
246:       ret = vp_form_parse(g_request + req.header_len, req.content_length,
247:                           &cred);
248:       if (ret < 0)
249:         {
250:           /* No detail about which field failed and no echo of what was typed:
251:            * the notice has to be useful to the person at the phone without
252:            * repeating a passphrase back over an open network.
253:            */
254: 
255:           len = vp_http_form_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
256:                                   "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 8-63 字节，"
257:                                   "请检查后重试。");
258:           if (len > 0)
259:             {
260:               /* Reuse the form page body but answer 400, so a client that
261:                * checks the status still learns the submit failed.
262:                */
263: 
264:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 400,
265:                                         "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 "
266:                                         "8-63 字节。");
267:             }
268:         }
269:       else
270:         {
271:           cred.generation = vp_store_next_generation(g_server.store_path);
272:           ret = vp_store_save(g_server.store_path, &cred);
273:           if (ret < 0)
274:             {
275:               *saved = false;
276:               *save_status = ret;
277:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 500,
278:                                         "写入持久存储失败，凭据未保存。");
279:             }
280:           else
281:             {
282:               *saved = true;
283:               *save_status = 0;
284:               *generation = cred.generation;
285:               len = vp_http_saved_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
286:                                        cred.ssid, cred.generation,
287:                                        cred.open_network);
288:             }
289:         }
290:     }
291: 
292:   if (len > 0)
293:     {
294:       (void)vp_write_all(fd, g_response, len);
295:     }
296: }
297: 
298: static void *vp_thread(void *arg)
299: {
300:   (void)arg;
301: 
302:   for (; ; )
303:     {
304:       struct pollfd pfd;
305:       uint32_t generation = 0;
306:       int save_status = 0;
307:       bool saved = false;
308:       bool stopping;
309:       int fd;
310:       int ret;
311: 
312:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
313:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
314:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
315:       if (stopping)
316:         {
317:           break;
318:         }
319: 
320:       pfd.fd = g_server.listenfd;
321:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
322:       pfd.revents = 0;
323: 
324:       /* Polling rather than blocking in accept(): stop() then needs no signal
325:        * and no socket shutdown trick that may or may not wake accept on a
326:        * given stack.
327:        *
328:        * This requires CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG on NuttX, which the Kconfig
329:        * depends on.  Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a
330:        * listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout
331:        * at all -- measured on the board as a service that reported
332:        * "listening" and then answered nothing.
333:        */
334: 
335:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
336:       if (ret < 0)
337:         {
338:           if (errno == EINTR)
339:             {
340:               continue;
341:             }
342: 
343:           break;
344:         }
345: 
346:       if (ret == 0)
347:         {
348:           continue;
349:         }
350: 
351:       fd = accept(g_server.listenfd, NULL, NULL);
352:       if (fd < 0)
353:         {
354:           if (errno == EINTR || errno == ECONNABORTED)
355:             {
356:               continue;
357:             }
358: 
359:           break;
360:         }
361: 
362:       vp_handle(fd, &saved, &save_status, &generation);
363: 
364:       /* Close before notifying.  The application is expected to leave SoftAP
365:        * from the callback, and doing that with the response still in flight is
366:        * what makes a successful save look like a failed submit on the phone.
367:        */
368: 
369:       shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
370:       close(fd);
371: 
372:       if (saved)
373:         {
374:           pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
375:           g_server.generation = generation;
376:           pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
377:         }
378: 
379:       if (saved || save_status < 0)
380:         {
381:           if (g_server.on_saved != NULL)
382:             {
383:               g_server.on_saved(save_status, generation, g_server.cb_arg);
384:             }
385:         }
386: 
387:       if (saved && g_server.one_shot)
388:         {
389:           break;
390:         }
391: 
392:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
393:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
394:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
395:       if (stopping)
396:         {
397:           break;
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
402:   if (g_server.listenfd >= 0)
403:     {
404:       close(g_server.listenfd);
405:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
406:     }
407: 
408:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_FINISHED;
409:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
410:   return NULL;
411: }
412: 
413: /* Caller holds g_lock. */
414: 
415: static void vp_reap_locked(void)
416: {
417:   if (g_server.state == VP_STATE_FINISHED)
418:     {
419:       pthread_t thread = g_server.thread;
420: 
421:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
422:       pthread_join(thread, NULL);
423:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
424:       g_server.state = VP_STATE_IDLE;
425:     }
426: }
427: 
428: int velasight_provisioning_start(
429:     const struct velasight_prov_config_s *config)
430: {
431:   struct velasight_prov_config_s cfg;
432:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
433:   pthread_attr_t attr;
434:   uint16_t port;
435:   int one = 1;
436:   int fd;
437:   int ret;
438: 
439:   memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
440:   if (config != NULL)
441:     {
442:       cfg = *config;
443:     }
444: 
445:   if (cfg.store_path != NULL &&
446:       strlen(cfg.store_path) >= VP_STORE_PATH_MAX)
447:     {
448:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
449:     }
450: 
451:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
452:   vp_reap_locked();
453:   if (g_server.state != VP_STATE_IDLE)
454:     {
455:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
456:       return -EALREADY;
457:     }
458: 
459:   port = cfg.port != 0 ? cfg.port :
460:          (uint16_t)CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT;
461: 
462:   fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
463:   if (fd < 0)
464:     {
465:       ret = -errno;
466:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
467:       return ret;
468:     }
469: 
470:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &one, sizeof(one));
471: 
472:   memset(&addr, 0, sizeof(addr));
473:   addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
474:   addr.sin_port        = htons(port);
475:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_ANY);
476: 
477:   if (bind(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0 ||
478:       listen(fd, 2) < 0)
479:     {
480:       ret = -errno;
481:       close(fd);
482:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
483:       return ret;
484:     }
485: 
486:   g_server.listenfd   = fd;
487:   g_server.stopping   = false;
488:   g_server.one_shot   = cfg.one_shot;
489:   g_server.generation = 0;
490:   g_server.on_saved   = cfg.on_saved;
491:   g_server.cb_arg     = cfg.cb_arg;
492:   snprintf(g_server.store_path, sizeof(g_server.store_path), "%s",
493:            cfg.store_path != NULL ? cfg.store_path :
494:            CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);
495: 
496:   pthread_attr_init(&attr);
497:   pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, VP_THREAD_STACK);
498:   ret = pthread_create(&g_server.thread, &attr, vp_thread, NULL);
499:   pthread_attr_destroy(&attr);
500:   if (ret != 0)
501:     {
502:       close(fd);
503:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
504:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
505:       return -ret;
506:     }
507: 
508:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_RUNNING;
509:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
510: 
511:   printf("provision_web: listening on 0.0.0.0:%u, store %s\n",
512:          (unsigned)port, g_server.store_path);
513:   return 0;
514: }
515: 
516: int velasight_provisioning_stop(void)
517: {
518:   pthread_t thread;
519: 
520:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
521:   vp_reap_locked();
522:   if (g_server.state != VP_STATE_RUNNING)
523:     {
524:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
525:       return -EALREADY;
526:     }
527: 
528:   g_server.stopping = true;
529:   thread = g_server.thread;
530: 
531:   /* Called from the saved callback, which runs on the listener thread: joining
532:    * ourselves would deadlock, so only ask the loop to end and let the normal
533:    * exit path close the socket.  A later stop() from the application reaps it.
534:    */
535: 
536:   if (pthread_equal(thread, pthread_self()))
537:     {
538:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
539:       return 0;
540:     }
541: 
542:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
543:   pthread_join(thread, NULL);
544: 
545:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
546:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_IDLE;
547:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
548:   return 0;
549: }
550: 
551: bool velasight_provisioning_is_running(void)
552: {
553:   bool running;
554: 
555:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
556:   running = g_server.state == VP_STATE_RUNNING;
557:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
558:   return running;
559: }
560: 
561: uint32_t velasight_provisioning_generation(void)
562: {
563:   uint32_t generation;
564: 
565:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
566:   generation = g_server.generation;
567:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
568:   return generation;
569: }
570: 
571: int velasight_provisioning_load_from(
572:     const char *path, struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out)
573: {
574:   if (path == NULL || out == NULL)
575:     {
576:       return -EINVAL;
577:     }
578: 
579:   return vp_store_load(path, out);
580: }
581: 
582: int velasight_provisioning_load(
583:     struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out)
584: {
585:   char path[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];
586: 
587:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
588:   if (g_server.store_path[0] != '\0')
589:     {
590:       snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s", g_server.store_path);
591:     }
592:   else
593:     {
594:       snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s", CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);
595:     }
596: 
597:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
598: 
599:   return velasight_provisioning_load_from(path, out);
600: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/provisioning_web_main.c
3:  *
4:  * A console front end for the provisioning service, for bringing it up by
5:  * hand on a board that has been switched into SoftAP.  Applications should
6:  * call velasight_provisioning_start() from their own long-lived task instead:
7:  * the listener runs on a pthread, and a pthread does not outlive the task that
8:  * created it, so a command that started the service and returned would take
9:  * the service with it.  That is why this command stays in the foreground.
10:  *
11:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
12:  ****************************************************************************/
13: 
14: #include <arpa/inet.h>
15: #include <errno.h>
16: #include <netinet/in.h>
17: #include <signal.h>
18: #include <stdbool.h>
19: #include <stdio.h>
20: #include <stdlib.h>
21: #include <string.h>
22: #include <sys/socket.h>
23: #include <sys/time.h>
24: #include <unistd.h>
25: 
26: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
27: 
28: static volatile bool g_interrupted;
29: 
30: static void provision_usage(void)
31: {
32:   printf("usage: provision_web [run [port] [--one-shot]] | selftest | show |"
33:          " path\n"
34:          "\n"
35:          "  run       serve the provisioning page until Ctrl-C.  port\n"
36:          "            defaults to %d.  --one-shot returns after the first\n"
37:          "            accepted save.\n"
38:          "  selftest  submit a canned form over loopback and verify it was\n"
39:          "            persisted.  Overwrites the stored record with a test\n"
40:          "            network; needs no phone.\n"
41:          "  show      print the stored network, never the passphrase\n"
42:          "  path      print the store path\n"
43:          "\n"
44:          "This service never changes the Wi-Fi role.  Put the board into\n"
45:          "SoftAP first (see docs/WiFi使用说明.md) and switch back afterwards.\n"
46:          "The page is plain HTTP with no authentication, so run it only while\n"
47:          "provisioning.\n",
48:          CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT);
49: }
50: 
51: static void provision_on_signal(int signo)
52: {
53:   (void)signo;
54:   g_interrupted = true;
55: }
56: 
57: static void provision_on_saved(int status, uint32_t generation, void *arg)
58: {
59:   (void)arg;
60: 
61:   if (status < 0)
62:     {
63:       printf("provision_web: save failed: %d\n", status);
64:       return;
65:     }
66: 
67:   printf("provision_web: credentials saved, generation %u\n",
68:          (unsigned)generation);
69: }
70: 
71: static int provision_show(void)
72: {
73:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
74:   int ret;
75: 
76:   ret = velasight_provisioning_load(&cred);
77:   if (ret == -ENOENT)
78:     {
79:       printf("provision_web: nothing provisioned at %s\n",
80:              CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);

158: /****************************************************************************
159:  * Name: provision_selftest
160:  *
161:  * Description:
162:  *   Drive the service over loopback on the board itself.  The host tests
163:  *   already cover the parsing and the record; what only the board can answer
164:  *   is whether this network stack accepts the listener and whether the SD-NAND
165:  *   write really lands.  Needs no phone, which matters because a Wi-Fi client
166:  *   is not always available when the firmware is.
167:  *
168:  *   It overwrites the stored record with an obvious test network.  The
169:  *   passphrase below is a fixed test string, never a real one.
170:  *
171:  ****************************************************************************/
172: 
173: #define PROV_TEST_PORT 18080
174: #define PROV_TEST_SSID "VelaSightProvTest"
175: #define PROV_TEST_PSK  "selftest-pass"
176: 
177: static int g_selftest_checks;
178: static int g_selftest_failures;
179: static volatile int g_selftest_cb_status = 1;
180: static volatile uint32_t g_selftest_cb_generation;
181: 
182: static void provision_check(bool ok, const char *what)
183: {
184:   g_selftest_checks++;
185:   if (!ok)
186:     {
187:       g_selftest_failures++;
188:     }
189: 
190:   printf("  %s %s\n", ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL", what);
191: }
192: 
193: static void provision_selftest_saved(int status, uint32_t generation,
194:                                      void *arg)
195: {
196:   (void)arg;
197:   g_selftest_cb_generation = generation;
198:   g_selftest_cb_status = status;
199: }
200: 
201: static int provision_exchange(const char *request, char *reply,
202:                               size_t replylen)
203: {
204:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
205:   struct timeval tv;
206:   size_t total = 0;
207:   int fd;
208: 
209:   fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
210:   if (fd < 0)
211:     {
212:       return -errno;
213:     }
214: 
215:   tv.tv_sec  = 5;
216:   tv.tv_usec = 0;
217:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
218:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
219: 
220:   memset(&addr, 0, sizeof(addr));
221:   addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
222:   addr.sin_port        = htons(PROV_TEST_PORT);
223:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
224: 
225:   if (connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0)
226:     {
227:       int error = -errno;
228: 
229:       close(fd);
230:       return error;
231:     }
232: 
233:   if (write(fd, request, strlen(request)) < 0)
234:     {
235:       int error = -errno;
236: 
237:       close(fd);
238:       return error;
239:     }
240: 
241:   for (; ; )
242:     {
243:       ssize_t n = read(fd, reply + total, replylen - 1 - total);
244: 
245:       if (n <= 0)
246:         {
247:           break;
248:         }
249: 
250:       total += (size_t)n;
251:       if (total >= replylen - 1)
252:         {
253:           break;
254:         }
255:     }
256: 
257:   close(fd);
258:   reply[total] = '\0';
259:   return (int)total;
260: }
261: 
262: static int provision_selftest(void)
263: {
264:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
265:   struct velasight_prov_config_s cfg;
266:   static char reply[2048];
267:   int waited;
268:   int ret;
269: 
270:   memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
271:   cfg.port     = PROV_TEST_PORT;
272:   cfg.on_saved = provision_selftest_saved;
273: 
274:   /* NuttX keeps this app's statics between invocations of the builtin, so a
275:    * second `provision_web selftest` would otherwise start with the previous
276:    * run's callback status already at 0 -- a pass inherited rather than
277:    * observed -- and report accumulated check counts.
278:    */
279: 
280:   g_selftest_checks = 0;
281:   g_selftest_failures = 0;
282:   g_selftest_cb_status = 1;
283:   g_selftest_cb_generation = 0;
284: 
285:   printf("provision_web selftest: loopback port %d, store %s\n",
286:          PROV_TEST_PORT, CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);
287: 
288:   ret = velasight_provisioning_start(&cfg);
289:   provision_check(ret == 0, "service starts on this network stack");
290:   if (ret < 0)
291:     {
292:       printf("provision_web selftest: start failed: %d\n", ret);
293:       return EXIT_FAILURE;
294:     }
295: 
296:   ret = provision_exchange("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n"
297:                            "Connection: close\r\n\r\n",
298:                            reply, sizeof(reply));
299:   provision_check(ret > 0 && strstr(reply, "200 OK") != NULL,
300:                   "GET / answers 200");
301:   provision_check(ret > 0 && strstr(reply, "name=\"ssid\"") != NULL &&
302:                   strstr(reply, "name=\"password\"") != NULL,
303:                   "the form carries both inputs");
304: 
305:   ret = provision_exchange("POST /save HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n"
306:                            "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
307:                            "\r\nContent-Length: 45\r\n\r\n"
308:                            "ssid=" PROV_TEST_SSID
309:                            "&password=" PROV_TEST_PSK,
310:                            reply, sizeof(reply));
311:   if (ret <= 0 || strstr(reply, "200 OK") == NULL)
312:     {
313:       /* Print the status line and the exchange result: a 500 here means the
314:        * store rejected the write, which on this board has meant a path the
315:        * VFAT could not represent.
316:        */
317: 
318:       printf("  submit result=%d, first line: %.*s\n", ret,
319:              (int)strcspn(reply, "\r"), reply);
320:     }
321: 
322:   provision_check(ret > 0 && strstr(reply, "200 OK") != NULL,
323:                   "the submit answers 200");
324:   provision_check(ret > 0 && strstr(reply, PROV_TEST_SSID) != NULL,
325:                   "the success page names the network");
326:   provision_check(ret > 0 && strstr(reply, PROV_TEST_PSK) == NULL,
327:                   "the success page does not echo the passphrase");
328: 
329:   for (waited = 0; waited < 50 && g_selftest_cb_status == 1; waited++)
330:     {
331:       usleep(100000);
332:     }
333: 
334:   provision_check(g_selftest_cb_status == 0,
335:                   "the saved callback reported success");
336:   provision_check(g_selftest_cb_generation > 0,
337:                   "the callback carried a generation");
338: 
339:   ret = velasight_provisioning_load(&cred);
340:   if (ret < 0)
341:     {
342:       printf("  load result=%d for %s\n", ret,
343:              CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);
344:     }
345: 
346:   provision_check(ret == 0, "the record reads back from persistent storage");
347:   if (ret == 0)
348:     {
349:       provision_check(strcmp(cred.ssid, PROV_TEST_SSID) == 0,
350:                       "the stored SSID matches what was submitted");
351:       provision_check(strcmp(cred.password, PROV_TEST_PSK) == 0,
352:                       "the stored passphrase matches what was submitted");
353:       provision_check(!cred.open_network, "the record is marked secured");
354:       provision_check(cred.generation == g_selftest_cb_generation,
355:                       "the stored generation matches the callback");
356:     }
357: 
358:   velasight_provisioning_stop();
359:   provision_check(!velasight_provisioning_is_running(),
360:                   "the service stops");
361: 
362:   printf("provision_web selftest: %s, %d checks, %d failures\n",
363:          g_selftest_failures == 0 ? "PASS" : "FAIL",
364:          g_selftest_checks, g_selftest_failures);
365:   printf("provision_web selftest: reboot and run `provision_web show` to "
366:          "confirm the record survives\n");
367:   return g_selftest_failures == 0 ? EXIT_SUCCESS : EXIT_FAILURE;
368: }

6: config LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_PROVISION_WEB
7: 	bool "AP-mode provisioning web entry"
8: 	default n
9: 	depends on NET_TCP && NET_TCPBACKLOG
10: 	---help---
11: 		A minimal HTTP server that serves one form, accepts an SSID and a
12: 		passphrase, and writes them to persistent storage.  Meant to be
13: 		started by the application through
14: 		velasight_provisioning_start() once the radio is already in
15: 		SoftAP; it never changes the Wi-Fi role itself, so the
16: 		application stays in control of when the network may drop.
17: 
18: 		NET_TCPBACKLOG is required, not merely nice to have.  Without it
19: 		NuttX reports no poll event for a pending connection on a
20: 		listening socket (TCP_BACKLOG is the only source of POLLIN
21: 		there), and accept() blocks with no timeout, so a listener that
22: 		can still be stopped is impossible.  The observed symptom of
23: 		building without it is a service that reports "listening" and
24: 		then never answers a request.
25: 
26: 		The provision_web command is the manual front end for bringing
27: 		it up over the console.
28: 
29: 		The page is plain HTTP with no authentication, which is the usual
30: 		trade-off for a provisioning page on an access point.  Run it
31: 		only while provisioning.
32: 
33: if LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_PROVISION_WEB
34: 
35: config VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE
36: 	string "Provisioning record path"
37: 	default "/mnt/sdnand/prov/wifi.bin"
38: 	---help---
39: 		Where the credential record is written.  The default is on
40: 		SD-NAND because that is the only persistent filesystem: /mnt is
41: 		pseudo-filesystem and /mnt/ram is a PSRAM ramdisk.  The parent
42: 		directory is created on demand.
43: 
44: 		Every path component must fit 8.3.  That SD-NAND is VFAT without
45: 		long-name support (CONFIG_FAT_LFN is not set), which rejects a
46: 		"velasight" directory or a "wifi-provision.bin" file with
47: 		-EINVAL rather than shortening it.
48: 
49: 		The passphrase is stored in the clear: VFAT has no permission
50: 		model to rely on and this part has no confirmed device key.  It
51: 		is never logged and never echoed back over HTTP, but physical
52: 		access to the SD-NAND reveals it.

55: 	int "Provisioning HTTP port"
56: 	default 80
57: 	range 1 65535
58: 	---help---
59: 		The port used when the caller passes 0.  80 means a phone can
60: 		open http://<board-ip>/ with no port in the URL.

# Execution and data flow

## 1. VelaSight boot/autostart

The board starts VelaSight after both framebuffers are registered.

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c`

- Lines `423-437` conditionally call `velasight_autostart()`.
- This happens after framebuffer registration, at lines `389-443`.
- If startup fails, the board prints `velasight autostart failed`.

`velasight_autostart()` is implemented in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/velasight_main.c`

- Lines `25-31` create a task named `velasight`.
- The task stack is 8192 bytes.
- The task calls `vs_app_run()`.

The application enters the main runtime at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_app.c`

- Lines `349-370`: initialize runtime, display, input, and network.
- Lines `370-381`: open the network context and immediately request STA mode.
- Lines `383-387`: open the `ai_agent` client.
- Lines `389-429`: run the permanent input/display/network event loop.

The initial network mode is STA:

- `vs_app.c:358-362`
- `runtime.network.mode = VS_NET_STA`
- `runtime.network.state = VS_NET_DOWN`

The network task is deliberately not using the ordinary board network autostart path when VelaSight is enabled. The guard is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258_bringup.c:273-287`

The normal `bk7258_net_autostart()` call is inside:

```c
#ifndef CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_VELASIGHT
```

Therefore, in the active VelaSight image:

- `bk7258_net_autostart()` is skipped.
- Its built-in DHCP retry behavior is skipped.
- `vs_network_apply_sta()` becomes the active boot association/DHCP path.

This distinction is important because the ordinary board path does retry DHCP, while VelaSight does not.

- With `CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO`, it polls for a mounted SD-NAND filesystem for up to 700 attempts at 100 ms each.
- Maximum wait is approximately 70 seconds.
- If SD-NAND is unavailable, it returns `-ETIMEDOUT`.

### Credential selection

- Lines `40-105`: `vs_config_load_wifi()`.
- Lines `65-89`: the provisioning record is the runtime source of STA credentials.
- Lines `73-80`: successful record load populates the STA SSID/password.
- Lines `81-89`: `-ENOENT` causes fallback to Kconfig defaults; other errors except `-EBADMSG` are returned.
- Lines `91-104`: Kconfig defaults populate the STA and AP fields.

# SoftAP startup and address/DHCP configuration

The main implementation is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_network.c`

## AP radio setup

`vs_network_apply_ap()` begins at line `164`.

### Validation

- Lines `172-174`: rejects an empty AP SSID and channels outside 1–14.

### Interface restart

- Lines `176-182`:
  - `wapi_set_ifdown(network->sock, "wlan0")`
  - `wapi_set_ifup(network->sock, "wlan0")`

An `-ENODEV` from `ifdown` is explicitly ignored at lines `176-178`.

### Master/AP mode

- Lines `184-198`: fill `struct wpa_wconfig_s`.
- `wifi.ifname = "wlan0"`
- `wifi.sta_mode = WAPI_MODE_MASTER`
- Channel is set via:
  - `wifi.freq = network->config.ap_channel`
  - `wifi.flag = WAPI_FREQ_FIXED`
- SSID and passphrase are passed to the WAPI/WEXT driver.

The actual WEXT association path is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/wireless/wapi/src/driver_wext.c`

- Lines `231-263`: create a socket and set the wireless mode.
- Lines `265-281`: configure WPA version and cipher.
- Lines `283-293`: configure fixed frequency.
- Lines `295-306`: set the encryption key.
- Lines `308-316`: set the ESSID.

Failure of `wpa_driver_wext_associate()` is logged as:

- `vs_network.c:200-204`
- Prefix: `velasight: network AP start failed: ...`

## AP address

The application hardcodes:

```c
address.s_addr = htonl(0xc0a80a01);
netmask.s_addr = htonl(0xffffff00);
```

at:

- `vs_network.c:207-208`

That is `192.168.10.1/24`.

The address is applied at:

- `vs_network.c:209-214`
- `netlib_set_ipv4addr("wlan0", &address)`

The netmask is applied at:

- `vs_network.c:216-220`
- `netlib_set_ipv4netmask("wlan0", &netmask)`

The underlying NuttX address helper is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/netlib/netlib_setipv4addr.c:59-88`

It performs `SIOCSIFADDR` on the interface.

## DHCP startup

The application starts DHCP at:

- `vs_network.c:223-228`

```c
ret = dhcpd_start("wlan0");
```

On success:

- `network->dhcp_running = true` at line `230`.

The generated configuration currently agrees with the hardcoded application address:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config`

- Line `3028`: DHCP start address
- Line `3029`: DHCP router address
- Line `3030`: DHCP netmask
- Line `3027`: maximum leases

The current values are the equivalent of:

- Router: `192.168.10.1`
- Netmask: `255.255.255.0`
- Pool starting at `192.168.10.2`
- Four leases

The DHCP API implementation is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c`

- Lines `1721-1751`: `dhcpd_start()`.
- It checks whether a DHCP daemon PID exists.
- It creates a task.
- It returns success as soon as `task_create()` succeeds.

The worker does the actual listener setup later:

- `dhcpd.c:1593-1616`: allocate daemon state and mark it running.
- `dhcpd.c:1620-1631`: call `dhcpd_openlistener()`.
- `dhcpd.c:1439-1488`: obtain interface address and bind UDP port 67.

### Important startup weakness

`dhcpd_start()` does not wait for the worker to:

- obtain the interface address,
- bind UDP port 67,
- or remain alive.

Thus `vs_network_apply_ap()` can mark the AP ready even if the DHCP worker immediately fails at:

- `dhcpd.c:1626-1631`
- for example, because the interface address is not visible yet or UDP port 67 is already occupied.

The application then prints:

- `vs_network.c:251-252`: `velasight: SoftAP ready...`

even though a phone may not obtain an address.

The repository documentation explicitly calls out repeated DHCP-start conflicts:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/WiFi使用说明.md:134-139`

It advises manually stopping DHCP before starting it again. The VelaSight application does not perform a worker-readiness check.

## DHCP stop

`vs_network_stop_dhcp()` is:

- `vs_network.c:33-46`

It calls `dhcpd_stop()` only if the application believes `network->dhcp_running` is true.

The underlying implementation:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c`

- Lines `1767-1794`: locate the daemon, send the wakeup signal, and `waitpid()` it.
- Lines `1557-1563`: the signal handler sets `DHCPD_STOP_REQUESTED`.
- Lines `1700-1705`: the worker frees state and resets its PID/state.

### Possible start/stop race

There is a timing gap:

1. `dhcpd_start()` creates the task and returns.
2. The child has not necessarily executed `dhcpd_run()` yet.
3. The application may immediately discover a provisioning startup failure and call `dhcpd_stop()`.
4. `dhcpd_stop()` may see no registered PID yet and return without stopping the just-created worker.

Relevant lines:

- `vs_network.c:223-240`
- `vs_network.c:257-260`
- `dhcpd.c:1729-1749`
- `dhcpd.c:1599-1616`
- `dhcpd.c:1771-1791`

This is a suspicious lifecycle race, particularly if port 80 is already occupied and AP setup enters the failure cleanup immediately after `dhcpd_start()`.

# Provisioning web startup and listener lifecycle

The reusable server is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/provisioning_web/vp_server.c`

The public API is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/provisioning_web/include/velasight_provisioning.h`

The header explicitly states that the web component does not manage Wi-Fi:

- `velasight_provisioning.h:4-9`
- It does not call WAPI, `ifup`, `ifdown`, DHCPD, or switch to STA.

## AP integration

After DHCP startup:

- `vs_network.c:230`: mark DHCP as running.
- `vs_network.c:231-235`: configure provisioning:
  - `one_shot = true`
  - callback = `vs_network_provision_saved`
  - callback argument = the VelaSight network object
- `vs_network.c:235`: call `velasight_provisioning_start()`.
- `vs_network.c:242`: mark provisioning as running.
- `vs_network.c:244-255`: set AP status and print the SoftAP-ready log.

The AP sequence is therefore:

1. Stop/bring up `wlan0`.
2. Configure WAPI master mode.
3. Associate/start beacon.
4. Assign `192.168.10.1/24`.
5. Start DHCPD.
6. Bind the HTTP listener.
7. Mark the UI state as AP ready.

## Listener bind and thread creation

`velasight_provisioning_start()`:

- `vp_server.c:428-514`

Important steps:

- `vp_server.c:451-457`: lock global singleton state and reject a second active server with `-EALREADY`.
- `vp_server.c:459-460`: select configured port, default 80.
- `vp_server.c:462-467`: create TCP socket.
- `vp_server.c:470`: request `SO_REUSEADDR`, ignoring its return value.
- `vp_server.c:472-475`: bind to `INADDR_ANY`, port selected.
- `vp_server.c:477-483`: bind/listen failure returns negative `errno`.
- `vp_server.c:486-494`: copy listener configuration into the singleton.
- `vp_server.c:496-505`: create the listener pthread.
- `vp_server.c:508-513`: set state to running and print:

```text
provision_web: listening on 0.0.0.0:<port>, store <path>
```

### Runtime `-114` finding

The runtime log is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/logs/runtime/provision-status-check-20260819-154004.log`

- Line `1`: `provision_web run 18080 --one-shot`
- Line `2`: `provision_web: start failed: -114`

`-114` is `-EALREADY` on this platform.

This failure is generated by the singleton state guard at:

- `vp_server.c:451-457`

It is not necessarily a bind failure on port 18080. The server refuses any second instance regardless of port. The likely state is:

- VelaSight already started its automatic one-shot provisioning server on port 80.
- The manual `provision_web run 18080 --one-shot` command attempted to start another instance.
- The singleton rejected it before creating/binding the second socket.

This is the clearest explanation of the observed `provision_web: start failed: -114`.

The relevant application design documentation confirms that VelaSight itself starts the server in AP mode:

- `vs_network.c:231-242`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/VELASIGHT_MCU_APP_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:11-13`
- `app/provisioning_web/README.md:42-50`

The manual command and automatic application path therefore conflict operationally.

## Accept loop

`vp_thread()` is:

- `vp_server.c:298-410`

Lifecycle:

1. Read `g_server.stopping`.
2. Poll the listener for 200 ms.
3. Accept one connection.
4. Serve exactly one request.
5. Shut down and close the connection.
6. Invoke the save callback, if applicable.
7. Exit after a successful save in one-shot mode.
8. Otherwise continue polling.

The poll dependency is intentionally documented:

- `vp_server.c:324-333`
- `app/provisioning_web/Kconfig:18-24`

`CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y` is enabled:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config:1153`

## Request and client-disconnect behavior

Request reading:

- `vp_server.c:105-189`
- 200 ms polling intervals.
- Five-second request deadline.
- Header/body size cap.
- Peer EOF is handled at lines `171-184`.
- Incomplete peer disconnect returns `-ECONNRESET`.

Request handling:

- `vp_server.c:201-296`
- GET page, rejected request, form validation, record save, and response generation.
- The response is written at lines `292-295`.

After handling:

- `vp_server.c:369-370`: `shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR)` and `close(fd)`.
- `vp_server.c:379-385`: invoke callback after the connection is closed.
- `vp_server.c:387-390`: successful one-shot save exits the thread.

The callback ordering is deliberate and documented:

- `velasight_provisioning.h:59-67`
- `app/provisioning_web/README.md:54-59`

The intended order is:

1. Save credentials.
2. Generate/write success response.
3. Close the client connection.
4. Notify the application.
5. Allow the application to switch from AP to STA.

This prevents the AP transition from cutting off the phone's success page.

# AP-to-STA transition and save handling

## Save callback

The VelaSight callback is:

`vs_network.c:71-84`

It does not directly change Wi-Fi mode. It:

- locks `event_lock`,
- records save status,
- marks `provision_event`,
- unlocks.

The main VelaSight loop consumes this event:

- `vs_app.c:392-410`
- `vs_network_process_events()` is called on every loop iteration.
- A successful save leads to `vs_network_request_mode(network, VS_NET_STA)`.

## Event consumption

`vs_network_consume_saved()`:

- `vs_network.c:86-112`

Behavior:

- Reads and clears the pending callback event under `event_lock`.
- Failed save:
  - returns `-ENOENT` if failure is being ignored during manual exit,
  - otherwise returns the failure status.
- Successful save:
  - reloads the persisted credentials,
  - replaces `network->config`.

## AP-to-STA transition

`vs_network_request_mode()`:

- `vs_network.c:308-366`

For AP to STA:

1. Set status to switching.
2. Stop the provisioning server:
   - lines `318-326`
3. Consume a completed save:
   - lines `328-339`
4. Stop DHCP:
   - lines `341-347`
5. Set internal mode to STA before association:
   - lines `352-356`
6. Apply STA mode:
   - lines `358-359`
7. Set error state on failure:
   - lines `360-364`

The cleanup ordering is generally correct: the HTTP response is complete and the listener is joined before DHCP/Wi-Fi teardown.

## Failure behavior

AP setup failure uses:

- `vs_network.c:257-261`

It attempts:

1. Stop provisioning.
2. Stop DHCP.
3. Bring `wlan0` down.

However, the cleanup return values are discarded. If either stop operation fails, the function returns the original setup error and does not report whether resources actually remained active.

The application-level close path also discards provisioning-stop errors:

- `vs_network.c:401-413`

It only prints a warning if DHCP stop fails at line `408`.

---

# STA startup and reconnect behavior

## STA startup

`vs_network_apply_sta()`:

- `vs_network.c:114-162`

Sequence:

1. Reject empty STA SSID:
   - lines `119-120`
2. `ifdown wlan0`:
   - lines `122-124`
3. `ifup wlan0`:
   - lines `126-128`
4. Configure managed-mode WPA:
   - lines `130-143`
5. Associate:
   - lines `145-147`
6. Obtain DHCP address:
   - lines `149-151`
7. Mark STA ready:
   - lines `153-161`

The DHCP call is only made once.

The observed runtime failure is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/logs/runtime/velasight-wpa-fix-boot-20260819-144933.log`

- Line `83`: interface request.
- Lines `84-90`: WPA state transitions and scan.
- Line `91`: `ap0: velasight: network STA DHCP failed: -1`
- Lines `94-127`: repeated scans continue.

This is consistent with the documented platform behavior:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/WiFi使用说明.md:34-37`

The first DHCP request after association can fail and a retry is normally required.

The board-level non-VelaSight path already implements retries:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_net_autostart.c`

- Lines `27-31`: explains the measured first-request failure.
- Lines `62-68`: three tries, 1.5-second gap.
- Lines `170-195`: retry loop.
- Lines `182-185`: success reporting.
- Lines `193-194`: retry logging.

But that function is skipped in the VelaSight build, as described above.

### Confirmed suspicious bug: no STA DHCP retry

`vs_network_apply_sta()` should be considered the direct source of the observed failure:

- `vs_network.c:145-151`

It:

- associates once,
- performs DHCP once,
- transitions to error immediately on the expected first-attempt timing failure,
- leaves no automatic retry or backoff.

This is more serious than a documentation-only issue because the product app bypasses the already-existing retry implementation.

## Disconnect/reconnect handling

There is no VelaSight-level Wi-Fi disconnect/reconnect state machine.

The application contains no handling in `vs_network.c` for:

- link-down events,
- association-lost events,
- DHCP lease renewal,
- reconnect callbacks,
- retry timers,
- interface-running state changes,
- AP client association/disassociation events.

`vs_network.c` only performs association when:

- the app boots into STA,
- the UI requests a mode switch,
- a saved provisioning event causes AP-to-STA transition.

The main loop only processes provisioning-save events:

- `vs_app.c:392-410`
- `vs_network_process_events()` does not inspect interface state.

The underlying WPA implementation may continue scanning internally, as shown by the runtime log, but the VelaSight application does not translate that into:

- a new DHCP attempt,
- a new ready/error state,
- or a UI reconnect result.

The project status explicitly acknowledges incomplete repeated-switching/stability coverage:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/SKILLS.md:124-126`

- STA is marked as passed for basic association/DHCP/TLS.
- SoftAP data-plane, repeated switching, and stability are still pending.

# Suspicious bugs and weaknesses

## 1. Confirmed STA DHCP retry omission

**Severity: high**

Files:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_network.c:145-151`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_net_autostart.c:170-195`

The normal board network path retries DHCP, but the active VelaSight path performs only one request. The runtime log shows exactly the resulting failure:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/logs/runtime/velasight-wpa-fix-boot-20260819-144933.log:91`

## 2. DHCP start is asynchronous and not health-checked

**Severity: high**

Files:

- `vs_network.c:223-251`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c:1721-1751`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c:1620-1631`

`dhcpd_start()` returning success only means the task was created. It does not mean UDP port 67 was bound or that the worker stayed alive. VelaSight prints `SoftAP ready` without checking actual DHCP readiness.

## 3. Potential DHCP start/stop race during AP failure cleanup

**Severity: medium/high**

Files:

- `vs_network.c:223-240`
- `vs_network.c:257-260`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c:1599-1616`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/netutils/dhcpd/dhcpd.c:1771-1791`

The worker may not have published its PID/state before `dhcpd_stop()` checks it. A failed HTTP bind immediately after DHCP startup could leave a newly created DHCP worker alive or leave stale state behind.

## 4. Hardcoded application AP address duplicates DHCP Kconfig

**Severity: medium**

Files:

- `vs_network.c:207-220`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config:3027-3030`

The application hardcodes the interface address and netmask while DHCP's pool/router/netmask come from Kconfig. They currently agree, but changing the Kconfig values without changing `vs_network.c` would produce inconsistent leases or gateway information.

## 5. Manual `provision_web` command conflicts with the automatic VelaSight server

**Severity: medium; directly explains runtime evidence**

Files:

- `vs_network.c:231-242`
- `vp_server.c:451-457`
- `provisioning_web_main.c:137-141`
- Runtime log: `provision-status-check-20260819-154004.log:1-2`

The server is a process-global singleton. A second instance is rejected with `-EALREADY` even if it requests a different port. The application automatically starts the server in AP mode, so running `provision_web run 18080 --one-shot` while VelaSight is in AP mode produces the observed `-114`.

There is no CLI command to attach to, inspect, or reconfigure the already-running application-owned server.

## 6. Listener death can leave VelaSight reporting AP ready

**Severity: medium/high**

Files:

- `vp_server.c:335-359`
- `vp_server.c:401-410`
- `vs_network.c:242-255`
- `vs_app.c:392-410`

Unexpected poll or accept errors break the listener thread. The server changes to `VP_STATE_FINISHED`, but VelaSight does not poll `velasight_provisioning_is_running()`. It only handles save events. The UI can therefore remain in the AP-ready state with no functioning HTTP listener.

## 7. Listener startup state race

**Severity: medium**

Files:

- `vp_server.c:496-509`

The sequence is:

1. `pthread_create()`
2. listener thread begins
3. parent later sets `g_server.state = VP_STATE_RUNNING`

If the thread exits immediately because of a poll/listener error, it can set `VP_STATE_FINISHED` at lines `401-409`, after which the parent can overwrite the state with `VP_STATE_RUNNING` at line `508`.

This is an unlikely normal-path race but is a real lifecycle weakness.

## 8. Concurrent start/stop/reap can join the same pthread twice

**Severity: medium**

Files:

- `vp_server.c:413-425`
- `vp_server.c:451-457`
- `vp_server.c:516-548`

`vp_reap_locked()` unlocks `g_lock` while performing `pthread_join()`. Another concurrent `start()` or `stop()` can observe `VP_STATE_FINISHED` and attempt to join the same thread simultaneously. The API is effectively singleton and expected to be used serially, but the implementation does not enforce serialized joins.

## 9. Save callback fires even if response transmission failed

**Severity: medium**

Files:

- `vp_server.c:292-295`
- `vp_server.c:369-385`

`vp_write_all()` returns errors such as `-EPIPE`, but its return value is ignored. If the phone disconnects after submitting valid credentials but before receiving the response:

- credentials are saved,
- the connection is closed,
- the save callback still fires,
- VelaSight may immediately leave SoftAP.

This is not data loss—the save succeeded—but it violates the intended “response delivered before callback” guarantee if “delivered” means successful socket write rather than merely attempted write.

## 10. `provision_web run` does not reset its interrupt flag

**Severity: medium**

Files:

- `provisioning_web_main.c:28`
- `provisioning_web_main.c:51-55`
- `provisioning_web_main.c:133-155`

`g_interrupted` is set by SIGINT but never reset at the beginning of `provision_run()`. Since the code itself notes that NuttX builtin statics persist between invocations:

- `provisioning_web_main.c:274-283`

a second `provision_web run` after Ctrl-C can start the listener and immediately exit because `g_interrupted` remains true.

## 11. Listener is exposed on every IPv4 interface

**Severity: security/design concern**

Files:

- `vp_server.c:472-475`
- `vp_server.c:511-512`
- `app/provisioning_web/README.md:181-187`

The server binds to `INADDR_ANY`, not specifically to the AP address. If invoked while STA is active, the unauthenticated plaintext HTTP provisioning endpoint may be reachable through the STA network as well as the SoftAP. The documentation acknowledges that the service has no authentication, but the implementation does not enforce AP-only operation.

## 12. AP address is hidden in application status/UI

**Severity: low/medium usability**

Files:

- `vs_network.c:253-255`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_display.c:195-202`

The actual address configured is `192.168.10.1`, but the status field and UI display a masked placeholder. The HTTP server prints `0.0.0.0:<port>`, and the application UI does not provide the actual address. This may be intentional for the submitted/reviewed code, but it makes direct device testing difficult and creates a mismatch between actual network configuration and displayed state.

# Bottom line

The two most important findings are:

1. The observed `velasight: network STA DHCP failed: -1` is consistent with a known first-DHCP timing failure, but the active VelaSight path performs no retry. The existing retry implementation is bypassed when VelaSight is enabled.

2. The observed `provision_web: start failed: -114` is generated by the provisioning server's process-global singleton state guard, not necessarily by port 18080. VelaSight automatically owns a one-shot listener in AP mode, so a manual `provision_web run 18080 --one-shot` invocation while that listener is active is rejected as already running.

The repository has good host-level coverage for the HTTP parser, storage, callback ordering, and basic listener lifecycle, but it has no automated coverage for the actual SoftAP/DHCP path, AP/STA transition repetition, DHCP worker readiness, Wi-Fi disconnect/reconnect, or the listener lifecycle races identified above.
